rationale: This is a template clone of the archived "Dual-Market Distress Funding" (MIN of two financing flows scaled by assets, multiplied by RANK(NEG(oancf/at))) with only dltr substituted for sstk, so despite the plausible gross-rollover story it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Internally consistent (both legs are increasing in the "recovery" direction, matching the positive expected sign) and a genuine change-based reframing of the archived "Recovery-Funded Net Repayment," though it remains close to the well-known net-external-financing anomaly and its cash-flow-improvement leg overlaps with cash-flow/profitability momentum.

The repayment share dltr/(dltr+dltis) is by construction one minus the issuance share, so this is essentially a sign-flip of the archived "Tax-Exhausted Debt Issuance" combined with the same tax-capacity leg, and the low-pi/low-txt conditioning loads on unprofitable firms whose known negative return tilt (and FF5 RMW exposure) works against the stated positive sign.

The MIN(sstk, dltr) matched equity-for-debt recapitalization leg is a genuinely new construct relative to the archived "Equity-Funded Earnings Repair," but the conditioning leg is identical and DELTA(re)/lagged assets is close to a mechanical ROA-minus-payout measure, so much of the predictive content may simply be the profitability effect.

A one-term addition to the archived "Uncovered Debt Service Gap" that also introduces a sign conflict — the dominant dltr−dltis component is net debt repayment, which the literature and this archive ("Cash-Backed Distress Deleveraging," fmb 2.92) associate with *higher* returns, contradicting the stated negative expected sign — while mixing a cash stock with financing flows on the same scale.

The acceleration (second-difference) of gross external financing is a construct not yet used in the archive and the sign is coherent with both the external-financing anomaly and the distress conditioning, though the RANK(NEG(re/at)) conditioner is heavily reused and ACCEL on annual financing flows is likely noisy with reduced coverage.
